validity.researcher_notes: P3299 = Vijaipur-Dadri Gas Pipeline (GREP-II), 48in x 505km, GAIL-owned, Vijaipur(Madhya Pradesh)->Dadri(Uttar Pradesh). EXISTENCE: real, confirmed by two independent origins. (1) GAIL's own 27-Nov-2018 letter to the regulator ('Final Tariff Determination of HVJ-GREP-DVPL and DVPL/GREP Upgradation Natural Gas Pipeline Network of GAIL (India) Limited', hosted at pngrb.gov.in as an official public-notice filing) states verbatim: 'For laying another 48" x 505 Km pipeline from Vijaipur to Dadri in parallel to the GREP in the same ROU, along with installation of new common compressors at Jhabua and Vijaipur (Phase-I)... As part of Phase-I, the 48" x 505 Km Vijaipur to Dadri pipeline was commissioned in March, 2010.' This is the DVPL-GREP Upgradation project's Phase-I, laid parallel to (and physically distinct from) the original 1997 GREP line (36in x 505km, = P3297/GREP-I). (2) offshore-technology.com's independent market-data profile ('Vijaipur-Dadri II gas pipeline, India', sourced from GlobalData's Oil & Gas Pipelines database, not GEM) separately states: 505km length, max diameter 48in, start year 2010, owner/operator GAIL (India), Madhya Pradesh->Uttar Pradesh. The two origins (a company regulatory filing vs. a commercial trade-press/GlobalData database) are independent of GEM and of each other and agree exactly on length, diameter, start year, route and operator -> tier=high. This also re-verifies the sheet's own cited leg (gem.wiki's reference list for this page points at this same PNGRB tariff filing and at PNGRB's data-bank page) -- checks out. CLASSIFICATION: correctly transmission (large-diameter, long-haul gas trunk line parallel to HVJ/GREP-I feeding the same downstream network); Fuel=Gas -- no dispute. DUPLICATE CHECK vs the 35-pipeline India-gas roster: P3299 is NOT a duplicate/relabel of P3297 (GREP-I). GAIL's letter itself distinguishes the original 1997 GREP line (36in x 505km, Vijaipur-Dadri, subsumed into HVJ-GREP) from the 2010 Upgradation Phase-I line (48in x 505km, Vijaipur-Dadri, laid 'in parallel to the GREP in the same ROU') -- two physically distinct, parallel pipes sharing a corridor and identical length (505km, because they run the same route) but different diameters and commissioning dates. This matches the orchestrator's guidance that GEM's HVJ/GREP/DVPL family is a real granularity split, not a double-count -- and specifically explains why P3297 and P3299 share an identical length figure without being the same asset. ATTRIBUTION: Owner GAIL (India) Ltd 100%, and endpoints Vijaipur(Madhya Pradesh)->Dadri(Uttar Pradesh), both confirmed by the same GAIL letter and by PNGRB's current 31-May-2026 NGPL MIS monthly report (https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf), which lists the combined 'Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur-GREP-Dahej-Vijaipur HVJ/VDPL Dadri' + 'Dahej-Vijaipur(DVPL)-Vijaipur-Dadri(GREP) Upgd. DVPL2 & VDPL' system under Entity=GAIL, traversing UP/MP/RJ/GJ/HR/DL/UK (states through which the constituent lines, including this one, pass). LENGTH/DIAMETER: 505km / 48in confirmed to the exact value by both independent sources -- no discrepancy. VERIFIER NOTE: the GAIL/PNGRB tariff-letter PDF is a SCANNED IMAGE with no text layer (confirmed: pdftotext extracts 0 lines) -- url_verifier correctly 200s but reports 'value not found' because it cannot OCR; I verified the content manually via pdftoppm (300dpi) + tesseract OCR and it reads exactly as quoted above. This is the same documented large/scanned-PDF false-negative flagged in the India country-scope note for PNGRB PDFs; the offshore-technology.com URL passes url_verifier's automated check cleanly.

validity.recommendation: Annotate in ResearcherNotes that Capacity=107.00 MMSCMD is the shared INTEGRATED-NETWORK total (HVJ+GREP-I+DVPL-I+GREP-II+DVPL-II combined), not GREP-II's own individual throughput, and that PNGRB's current (May 2026) edition shows the combined system capacity has since risen to 111.3 MMSCMD -- do not change the value or collapse the rows; this is the expected granularity/staleness artifact the orchestrator's scope note anticipated, and it is common to all five constituent GEM rows, not a P3299-specific defect.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's Capacity=107.00 MMSCMD on P3299 is NOT GREP-II's own individual capacity -- it is the combined capacity of the entire post-Upgradation 'Integrated HVJ' system, and the identical 107.0 value is stamped on all five constituent GEM rows (P0925 HVJ, P0919 DVPL-I, P3297 GREP-I, P3298 DVPL-II, P3299 GREP-II per the roster). Confirmed by two independent sources that both distinguish the segment-level contribution from the system-level figure: (1) GAIL's 2018 tariff letter gives GREP-II's (Phase-I's) own INCREMENTAL contribution as +11 MMSCMD, versus DVPL-II's (Phase-II's) +43 MMSCMD, summing with the pre-Upgradation base to reach the 107 network total rather than GREP-II standing alone at 107. (2) PNGRB's current 31-May-2026 NGPL MIS report lists 'Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur-GREP-Dahej-Vijaipur HVJ/VDPL Dadri' plus the DVPL2/VDPL Upgradation as ONE combined line item under a single Entity=GAIL row: 6,169km authorised / 6,732km operating / 111.3 MMSCMD authorised+determined capacity (up from the 107.0 MMSCMD figure GEM's sheet carries) -- never broken out by GEM's five separate ProjectIDs. This matches the orchestrator's scope note precisely: GEM's India CapacityBcm/y is derived from the regulator's SYSTEM-level MMSCMD figure at the time of research, so all five split rows inherited the same (now slightly stale) system total rather than a per-segment number, and the current PNGRB edition shows that total has grown ~4% (107.0 -> 111.3) since GEM's figure was set, consistent with ongoing debottlenecking/capacity augmentation rather than a unit or data-entry error. Per guidance I am NOT proposing to collapse GEM's rows or change the value -- flagging the caveat only, exactly mirroring the identical finding already staged on sibling row P3298 (DVPL-II).

summary: P3299 (GREP-II) is real, correctly classified/attributed, and not a duplicate of GREP-I; its 505km/48in/2010/GAIL/Vijaipur-Dadri figures are independently confirmed (GAIL's 2018 PNGRB tariff letter + offshore-technology.com), one spec caveat staged (Capacity=107 MMSCMD is the shared 5-row integrated-network total, now stale vs PNGRB's current 111.3 MMSCMD), and StartMonth1=March filled (medium tier, single source). No UNRESOLVED items.
